full_judgment:
6. The learned Judge, Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Bishesh Adalat 1, Nilphamari, upon consideration of the evidence of prosecution witnesses and documentary evidence on record, found the condemned prisoner guilty of the offence punishable under section 10(1) of Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Bishesh Bidhan Ain and sentenced the petitioner to death by his judgment and order dated 7-1-1999 and thereupon sent the records to the High Court Division under section 374 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for confirmation of sentence of death and the same was numbered as Death Reference No. 1 of 1999. The petitioner also filed Jail Appeal No. 364 of 1999 against the aforesaid judgment of the trial Court. The Death Reference and the Jail Appeal were heard together and the learned Judges of the High Court Division upon hearing the parties and on perusal of oral and documentary evidence on record accepted the Death Reference and dismissed the Jail Appeal by judgment and order dated 23-10-2002. 

 7. Mr Serajul Haq, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner, placed before us the judgment of the trial Court as well as the impugned judgment of the High Court Division and thereafter contended that the High Court Division committed an error of law in failing to consider that the PW 1, Mukbul Hossain, is the informant and father of the deceased Bilkis Banu, PW 3 Montaz Ali is the uncle and PW 6 Nazrul Islam is the brother of the deceased Bilkis and all these PWs are interested and partisan in nature and, as such, the order of conviction relying upon the evidence of the aforesaid witnesses cannot be sustained in law. He further contended that the prosecution failed to examine any independent and disinterested witnesses in support of the prosecution case. 

 8. Mr Serajul Haq lastly, contended that the learned Judges of the High Court Division erred in law in failing to consider that the prosecution purposely withheld some vital FIR-named witnesses such as Md Azizul, Mohiruddin and Jamiruddin, who are neighbours of the place of occurrence and for non-examination of those witnesses by the prosecution the appellant has been seriously prejudiced and he is entitled to get the benefit of section 114(g) of the Evidence Act and, in such view of the matter, the findings and decisions as arrived at by the High Court Division cannot be sustained in, law. 

 10. We have heard the learned Counsels and perused the judgment of the trial Court and the impugned judgment of the High Court Division. It appears that the trial Court after considering both oral and documentary evidence on record found the petitioner guilty for murdering his wife for dowry which is punishable under section 10(1) of Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Bishesh Bidhan Ain, 1995 and accordingly, passed the sentence of death. 

 11. We have read the impugned judgment of the High Court Division where from it appears that the learned Judges of the High Court Division have meticulously discussed and assessed both oral and documentary evidence in their proper perspective and held as follows: 

 "In the absence of any other proof of commission of murder of the wife in other way and the absence of explanation coming from the side of the husband of the wife for the murder of his wife in his custody, and it being proved by evidence that the condemned prisoner demanded dowry some days before murder of his wife and he returned angry and the report of post-mortem containing several injuries on the person of Bilkis Banu proving her death and fact of abscondence from the house on the occurrence of murder, being proved.
